findings.description: The implementation calculates the total weight using a sum over the records iterator and then iterates over the same iterator again to build the result dictionary. If records is a one-shot iterator (e.g., a generator), the second iteration operates on an exhausted iterator, resulting in an empty dictionary or incorrect results.
findings.evidence: Example: records = (("a", 1), ("b", 2)) as a generator. allocate(records, 10) returns {} instead of {"a": 4, "b": 6}.

review.summary: allocate consumes the records iterable twice, violating the one-shot iterator requirement.
